plain: A delay in carrying out a punishment, especially a death sentence.

webster.text: To respit after sentence of death; to suspend or delay the execution of for a time; as, to reprieve a criminal for thirty days.

more.text: The temporary suspension of the execution of sentence of death on a criminal.

example.quote: But the President may be at the head of a combination against the rights of the people, and may reprieve or pardon the whole.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. LENOIR, July 30, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
